capability_advanced: Original repository Starlark now reaches the inactive GeneralWorkspace native driver through typed reservation/operation Needs, executes actual processes, replays one ordered transcript, and adopts the same reserved root. Two retained cquery commands prove fresh process identities, nonzero side effects, subsequent reads/template/delete, and exactly-once ordered prints/process output using ASCII first/second captures. Separate event/frame/CLI-writer tests prove preservation of NUL and 0xff bytes. This is a bounded diagnostic-scope fixture; public authentic Rust remains open.

compatibility.exact_inherited: The pinned Bazel 9.2 repository API source contract remains the authority for argv/Path/Label, validation order, environment override/removal, cwd/quiet, Latin1 result projection and sequential file/process behavior. Existing accepted source/oracle evidence is inherited; no new Bazel oracle invocation or expanded platform/API parity claim.
compatibility.slug_native: Structural physical path spelling and identities, finite native quotas, confined read-only Linux Host view, command-fresh process sampling, JSON stderr byte arrays, and a new 64MiB serialized daemon-frame limit including newline. That limit also applies with General disabled and may refuse large ordinary query output.
compatibility.unsupported_deferred: Production per-command source scope, unbridged Local/legacy selected process sources, foreign materialization Path get_child/dirname, cross-root symlink operations, full archive envelope, non-Linux native source execution, original-route physical CAS/runfiles, public Rust and equivalent-command memory remain gated.

ownership: Reservations share their mandatory full expected RepoSpec Arc with native tickets. Stable display/slot hash excludes Spec; full equality, admission and bounded retention include Spec. Typed operation Needs carry independently selected complete current source associations, not transcript-owned source histories.

An ordinary DICE execution-policy key defaults Disabled. Core injects current policy and a fresh empty workspace epoch before reuse; trusted enablement requires an already installed Diagnostic source scope. Native production has no per-command source scope and cannot enable this candidate. Enabled refusals never fall back to caller profiles.

Original Loading uses one exact replay cursor for all admitted mutations, observations and Execute. Prefix source declarations start empty on each retry and register only real typed accesses. Own Labels resolve through the reserved root without a terminal materialization self-cycle. Generic path/read/listing producers retain materialization anchors; no Host fallback or above-anchor demand is introduced.

Canonical anchored source Legacy outputs discard captured frontiers on success/error while preserving child DICE dependencies; Observed outputs retain exact frontiers. Listing keys structurally include the complete optional anchor and explicitly refuse escapes. Host/legacy None behavior is protected.

All General workspace frontier metadata is checked before any native setup/effect. Current index, exact predecessor/completed record and full selected source associations are validated without predicting future snapshots. Enabled legacy execute/filesystem and terminal generated-effect frontiers refuse before effects.

One workspace bank persists across commands. Credited retirement custody spans mutable command drop, bootstrap builder and seed token, workers, queued/refused result delivery and standalone/renewed finalized native views. Driver waits the original cleanup deadline before observation restoration and lease close. Timeout/quarantine leaves Open/Busy with no early refund or cleanup-success claim; actual later retirement may release credits. Immutable readers retain data without mutation authority.

Completion-output events share captured stdout/stderr Arcs and key replay deduplication by actual lease/index. stdout precedes stderr with no inserted newline or text conversion. Need discards provisional batches; consistent completion including later Starlark failure retains output, while source/environment consistency or publication failure suppresses unverified output. Events, native publication, daemon wire and CLI stderr carry bytes; partial delivery failure is an output error.

Daemon input and response framing is capped before response-sized allocation; counting includes byte-array expansion and newline, malformed/incomplete/oversized requests close the connection, and response overflow uses a bounded error frame. No dependency, global interner/cache or cap increase was introduced.
